title: Consistency Pact
concept: A private weekly check on the gap between what you say you value and what you actually did, and one specific change to close it, without your partner having to check.
whenToUse: Once a week, on your own, to see whether you did what you said you would. Also after a promise that mattered, or alongside a shared Proof item while you rebuild trust.
steps: What you say — what do you say you value? Write it down.
What you meant to do — what did you plan to do this week?
What actually happened — where was the gap?
One change — pick one thing to do differently next week that you could point to.
Keep it private unless you choose to share it. It’s easier to be honest with yourself when it’s for your eyes only.
Not a substitute for repairing a real breach. If you broke something you agreed, tell your partner. This pact doesn’t replace that.

phrases.text: Next week I will ___ (something you could point to).

working: A’s sharp reply on Tuesday goes unrepaired until Thursday. A’s change for next week: a same-day text, “That was sharp, sorry.” By Friday A has sent one.
notWorking: B breaks an agreement about money and, instead of telling A, writes it up in a private pact. Writing it down is fine; hiding it from A isn’t. A private pact never replaces telling your partner.
activity: Write your own private pact. Check in on it once a week for three weeks.
